title: Yugong Moves the Mountains

source.quote: Though I die, my sons will live; sons beget grandsons, grandsons beget sons, sons beget more sons, sons beget more grandsons — generation after generation without end, while the mountains grow no taller. Why should they not be levelled?

moral: I cannot finish it, but my sons and their sons can — the mountains will not grow taller.

story.title: Two Mountains
story.text: Two mountains stood in front of Yugong's house. Going out meant a long detour.
story.narration: The mountains Taihang and Wangwu blocked Yugong's door. A single trip out meant days of walking around them.

story.title: Level the Mountains
story.text: Ninety-year-old Yugong said: let us level them together.
story.narration: Yugong, ninety years old, called his family together: these mountains have blocked us for generations. Let us level them — shall we?

keyMoment.question: Zhisou laughed: you are almost ninety — can you really finish?

options.text: I can't finish, so never mind
I can't finish, but my sons and their sons will — the mountains don't grow

keyMoment.reveal: Generation after generation without end, while the mountains grow no taller — the mountain cannot grow, but people go on.

misconceptions: If one person can't finish it, don't start
You are too old to do anything

quiz.question: Which two mountains stood in front of Yugong's house?
quiz.explanation: Taihang and Wangwu blocked the way out.

quiz.question: How did Yugong answer Zhisou's laughter?
options: I can't finish, but my sons and grandsons will, generation after generation
I will ask someone else to dig
quiz.explanation: The mountains will not grow taller, but people go on generation after generation.

quiz.question: Which of these is most like Yugong moving the mountains?
options: Reading a page a day and finishing a thick book in a year
Staying up all night to finish the book
Leaving the book because it is too hard
quiz.explanation: What one person cannot finish can be done slowly, and carried on.
